title: Frustration-Free Models for Topological Holography: Fusion Spin Chains as Boundary Algebras
abstract: We introduce a class of $2d$ quantum spin systems based on a unitary spherical fusion category with a chosen object. These models have frustration-free, reflection positive, but generally non-commuting local interactions, generalizing the Levin-Wen string-net models. Based on the theory developed in arXiv:2510.20662, we explicitly realize the Temperley-Lieb-Jones algebra, and more generally fusion spin chains as their boundary algebras.
summary: This work constructs a novel class of frustration-free quantum spin models for topological holography using unitary spherical fusion categories. By applying advanced mathematical techniques, the authors demonstrate that the boundary algebra of these 2D systems precisely realizes fusion spin chains. This provides a powerful algebraic framework for understanding topological order in correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop frustration-free quantum spin models for Topological Holography by realizing fusion spin chains as boundary algebras.
main_result: It proves that applying Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction to specific 2D quantum spin systems yields boundary algebras isomorphic to the fusion spin chains determined by the input unitary spherical fusion category.
method: The methodology involves constructing local Hamiltonians on lattices (like the honeycomb lattice) using fusion categories and then employing techniques like reflection positivity and OS reconstruction to determine the boundary structure.
model_or_system: The models are 2D quantum spin systems defined by a unitary spherical fusion category C and an object $\rho$. They generalize Levin-Wen string-net models and feature frustration-free, reflection positive local interactions.
key_observables: Topological order, ground-state degeneracy, anyonic excitations, and the structure of the boundary algebra.
important_parameters: The input unitary spherical fusion category C and the chosen object $\rho$.
main_assumptions: The models are assumed to be frustration-free and reflection positive; the existence of a uniform gap and the LTQO condition are noted as open questions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates two types of interactions (horizontal edge and rectangle) for a qubit system, while Figure 2 shows the colored honeycomb lattice structure.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the general 2D spin system based on a fusion category, detailing the local Hamiltonian construction on the honeycomb lattice, proving the ground state projection via evaluation maps, and finally analyzing the resulting boundary algebra structure using modular automorphism techniques.
why_interesting: The connection between abstract algebraic structures (fusion categories) and concrete physical models (spin chains) that exhibit topological order is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases in condensed matter systems.
